audits.mathematicalReason: Since P is the centroid, AP = 2PD = 4 and CP = 2PE = 3. Also, PE² + PD² = 1.5² + 2² = 2.5² = DE², so ∠EPD is a right angle by the converse of the Pythagorean theorem; perpendicularity is not assumed from the drawing. The four triangles APE, EPD, DPC, and CPA have areas 3, 1.5, 3, and 6, respectively. Their sum is 13.5. The assessed nodes and area-support nodes accurately describe this valid solution method.

audits.mathematicalReason: Each equal arc measures 360°/12 = 30°. The minor arc AE contains four increments, so ∠AOE = 120°. Equal radii make triangle AOE isosceles, giving x = 30°. The minor arc GI contains two increments, so ∠GOI = 60° and the isosceles triangle GOI gives y = 60°. Thus x + y = 90°. The alternative inscribed-angle route is also valid: A and G are opposite endpoints of a diameter, so x = ∠GAE intercepts a 60° arc and y = ∠AGI intercepts a 120° arc. Both optional routes are defensible without requiring their union.

routes.label: Divide the half-turn into equal wedges
Close the outer rim into a ten-gon

audits.mathematicalReason: Parallel bases make each smaller trapezoid angle 180° − x. Extending the legs inward forms congruent isosceles wedges with a common apex, since adjacent congruent trapezoids share a leg with matching inner and outer endpoints. Each wedge angle is 180° − 2(180° − x) = 2x − 180°. The nine wedges span the half-turn between the terminal horizontal edges, so 9(2x − 180°) = 180°, yielding x = 100°. The polygon route is independently valid: closing the nine-segment outer rim along the baseline makes a ten-gon. Its two endpoint angles are each 180° − x, and its eight other angles are each 2(180° − x). Thus 18(180° − x) = 8·180°, again giving 100°. The shared angle-operation scope and both route-specific scopes are appropriate.

figureEvidence.fact: The nine trapezoids form an unbroken arch with their shorter parallel bases facing inward. Adjacent pieces share nonparallel sides, and the two terminal bottom edges lie on the same horizontal baseline. The outer rim consists of nine segments.

audits.mathematicalReason: The two square widths total 30, while their union has width 25, so the overlap has width 5. Its height is 15, giving shaded area 75. Rectangle AQRD has area 15·25 = 375, so the shaded percentage is (75/375)·100% = 20%. Rectangle-area calculation and finding a percentage rate precisely match the proposed assessed scopes.

audits.mathematicalReason: Each coin has radius 2. The convex hull of the centers is a trapezoid whose bottom edge has length 8 and whose other three edges each have length 4, because neighboring touching centers are one diameter apart. Corresponding common tangent segments have the same lengths, so the straight portions total 20. The touching triples form equilateral triangles; the exposed corner arcs have central angles 120°, 120°, 60°, and 60°. Equivalently, these angles are the exterior turns of the center trapezoid and sum to 360°. Hence the arcs total one circumference, 2π·2 = 4π, and the band length is 20 + 4π centimeters. This validates the arc-length method and the stated tangent, equilateral-triangle, and exterior-angle support.

figureEvidence.fact: Three touching coins form the bottom row, and two touching coins are nestled in the gaps above them. The band follows four straight common-tangent portions joined by exposed arcs on the four corner coins.

audits.mathematicalReason: In a five-term arithmetic sequence, the third term is the arithmetic mean of the first and fifth. Therefore the top-row middle entry is (1 + 25)/2 = 13, and the bottom-row middle entry is (17 + 81)/2 = 49. Applying the same relationship to the middle column gives X = (13 + 49)/2 = 31. This directly matches the supplied arithmetic-mean definition and criteria; a general arithmetic-sequence formula is not necessary for this route.

figureEvidence.fact: The 5-by-5 array has corner entries 1 at the upper left, 25 at the upper right, 17 at the lower left, and 81 at the lower right. X occupies row 3, column 3.

routes.label: Place S and follow forced cells

audits.mathematicalReason: An explicit tiling has rows SSUU / VSSU / VVVU, where S is a reflected S tile and U and V are L tiles. Thus the proposed pair is achievable. To exclude the other choices, checkerboard coloring gives equal board color counts, while a T tile has color imbalance ±2 and I, O, L, S are balanced; this excludes B and E. Next color alternating columns. The board again has equal color counts. Under every rotation, reflection, or translation, an L tile has signed imbalance 2 modulo 4, whereas S and I have imbalance 0 modulo 4. Consequently a single L together with S and I, or with two S tiles, cannot cover the board, excluding A and D. These are necessary-condition exclusions followed by a construction, not an assumption that color balance alone guarantees a tiling. Direct placement checking is also a valid alternative. The combining-shapes scope and rotation/reflection support are defensible.

figureEvidence.fact: The displayed S consists of two offset rows of two squares. The L consists of three squares in a line with a fourth attached at an end; T has a three-square bar with a fourth attached at its middle. These silhouettes identify the pieces used in the construction and coloring checks.

audits.mathematicalReason: The original pattern is 5 by 5. Adding a one-tile-wide outside border makes it 7 by 7, adding 49 − 25 = 24 shaded tiles without changing the 17 unshaded tiles. The new shaded count is 8 + 24 = 32, so the requested shaded-to-unshaded ratio is 32:17. The ratio-meaning scope and elementary mixed-arithmetic support accurately describe this solution.
